name: Vd-17871 field (Hubble)
blurb: A deep field toward the starburst galaxy Vd-17871, seen by Hubble.
label: vd17871-hubble
story: Hidden in this field is Vd-17871, a distant starburst galaxy first picked out by its millimeter glow and later found to be a rotating disk. Hubble looked here to learn how massive galaxies formed and gathered dust within 1.5 billion years after the Big Bang.

claims.text: VD-17871 is one of three millimeter-identified z>4 starburst galaxies in the COSMOS field targeted by Hubble program 13294
Vd-17871 is a spectroscopically confirmed submillimeter galaxy at z = 4.622 in the COSMOS field, first identified at 1.2 mm
Vd-17871 shows regular gas rotation on kpc scales (a disk)
The program aims to understand massive galaxy formation and dust accumulation within 1.5 billion years after the Big Bang
